clause_positions.state_position: Capped at contract value, with carve-outs
clause_positions.proposed_position: Accept a cap at contract value, provided the carve-outs are listed and none is uncapped for data handling beyond our service-provider role.
clause_positions.rationale: A 1x cap is inside the 2x fallback. The carve-outs are not specified, so we ask for the list before agreeing.

clause_positions.state_position: Vendor indemnifies for IP infringement and third-party claims
clause_positions.proposed_position: Accept, excluding claims arising from state-supplied materials and from the Kansas state-owned assets supplied under Kansas's release.
clause_positions.rationale: Matches the fallback; adding the Kansas assets to the exclusion follows from the stage 3 IP clearance request.

clause_positions.proposed_position: State owns deliverables D1-D6; we receive a license back to generic components (design system patterns, tokens, research methods).
clause_positions.playbook_fallback: State owns deliverables; vendor gets license back to generic components
clause_positions.rationale: Equals the fallback and keeps KS-DS-01, KS-DS-02 and KS-RS-01 reusable for future bids.

clause_positions.proposed_position: Disclose all 13 Kansas assets used. For the 8 vendor-owned assets, grant a royalty-free perpetual license for state use. For the 5 state-owned assets, California's rights can only flow through Kansas's written release, which is still pending.
clause_positions.playbook_fallback: Royalty-free perpetual license for state use
clause_positions.rationale: The playbook assumes we own the pre-existing IP. We cannot license the 5 Kansas state-owned assets ourselves, so this falls outside the fallback until Kansas grants the release (Addendum Q1 requires the state to receive a license).

clause_positions.state_position: State has 30 days to accept each deliverable
clause_positions.proposed_position: 15 business days per deliverable with one rework cycle; deemed accepted if no response.
clause_positions.rationale: We open at the fallback rather than the preferred 10 days because payment depends on acceptance; if the state holds at 30 days, escalate to the delivery manager.

clause_positions.proposed_position: 10% withheld, released within 45 days of final acceptance of D6.
clause_positions.playbook_fallback: 10% withheld, released within 45 days of final acceptance
clause_positions.rationale: Matches the RFP's 10% withholding and adds a release date.

clause_positions.proposed_position: 60 days from acceptance of each deliverable.
clause_positions.rationale: At the fallback; a 90-day warranty would run past the 6-month term with no staff budgeted for it.

clause_positions.proposed_position: Payment for accepted deliverables plus work in progress at the rate card.
clause_positions.playbook_fallback: Pay for accepted deliverables + work in progress
clause_positions.rationale: Equals the fallback; the rate card gives an agreed basis for valuing work in progress.

clause_positions.state_position: Vendor protects state data; breach notice required
clause_positions.proposed_position: Breach notice within 72 hours; we act only as a service provider for any personal data, including usability test participants.
clause_positions.rationale: Our preferred position; adds the service-provider commitment required by C-09 for R-10 participant data.

clause_positions.proposed_position: Name the UX lead and delivery manager as key personnel; state approval of replacements with a 15-day window.
clause_positions.rationale: At the fallback. Naming the Kansas-experienced UX lead supports the 15% key-staff evaluation weight.

clause_positions.proposed_position: Change requests priced at the rate card; a written amendment only for scope changes over 5% of contract value.
clause_positions.playbook_fallback: Amendment for scope change over 5% of value
clause_positions.rationale: At the fallback. Gives a priced path for threshold languages beyond Spanish, whose scope is still open.

draft_sections.heading: 1. Agreement and order of precedence
draft_sections.text: This agreement, the General Provisions - Information Technology (GSPD-401IT), RFP SAMPLE-CA-HUX-2026-014 including Addendum 1, and the vendor's proposal apply in that order of precedence.

draft_sections.heading: 2. Statement of work and deliverables
draft_sections.text: The vendor delivers a UX enhancement of the apply, renew and document-upload journeys through deliverables D1 (discovery, month 1) to D6 (final specifications and handoff, month 6), meeting requirements R-01 to R-12 as set out in the trace matrix exhibit. The state build team implements the designs. The 6-month term starts at contract execution (Addendum Q3).

draft_sections.heading: 3. Payment schedule and withholding
draft_sections.text: The state pays on written acceptance of each deliverable: D1 10%, D2 15%, D3 20%, D4 20%, D5 15%, D6 20% of the fixed price. 10% of each payment is withheld and released within 45 days of final acceptance of D6.

draft_sections.heading: 4. Acceptance criteria and process
draft_sections.text: The state reviews each deliverable within 15 business days against its acceptance criteria and the compliance checks in the compliance matrix exhibit, with one rework cycle. A deliverable is deemed accepted if the state does not respond within that period.

draft_sections.heading: 5. Key personnel
draft_sections.text: Key personnel are the UX lead (EMP-104) and the delivery manager (EMP-166). Replacements require state approval within 15 days.

draft_sections.heading: 6. Intellectual property and licenses
draft_sections.text: The state owns deliverables D1-D6; the vendor receives a license back to generic components. The vendor discloses all pre-existing Kansas assets used and grants a royalty-free perpetual license to the 8 vendor-owned assets. Rights to the 5 Kansas state-owned assets (KS-JM-01, KS-JM-02, KS-UI-01, KS-UI-02, KS-LG-01) pass to California under the written release from Kansas, attached as an exhibit once received. [PENDING LEGAL - escalated at H5]

draft_sections.heading: 7. Privacy, security and data handling
draft_sections.text: No member health information is shown in notifications or page titles (R-08). The vendor follows state security policy (SAM 5300 / SIMM 5300), acts only as a service provider for any personal data, including usability participants, and notifies the state of any breach within 72 hours.

draft_sections.heading: 8. Special terms and exhibits
draft_sections.text: Exhibits: A - rate card (applies to change requests and termination); B - compliance matrix from the approved trace matrix; C - Kansas release (pending). Change requests are priced at the rate card; scope changes over 5% of contract value need a written amendment.

open_questions.question: Which carve-outs does the state attach to the liability cap, and are any uncapped?
open_questions.why_it_matters: An uncapped carve-out, for example for data breaches, could take the liability position outside the fallback.

open_questions.question: If Kansas has not granted the release by contract signature, do we sign with the IP section pending, or remove the 5 state-owned assets from scope and price the redesign?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the one clause escalated to legal; it decides whether signing can proceed on time.

rad_impacts.note: 10 of 11 clauses are within fallback; only pre-existing IP (Kansas assets) escalates, to legal and the UX lead.
Proposed acceptance of 15 business days with deemed acceptance, against the state's 30 days.
Legal approval is needed for one escalated clause, pre-existing IP.
The Kansas release now also blocks the IP section of the contract, not just the reuse baseline.
